mods.name: Armor Model API
mods.description: Renders Bedrock/GeckoLib geo armor models through the vanilla armor pipeline.

releases.notes:
# 1.1.2

- Minecraft 26.3 support
- Trims now use the game's paletted textures: each greyscale trim texture needs a `.png.mcmeta` with
  `{"palette": {"base_palette": "minecraft:trim_base"}}`, and `atlases/armor_trims.json` can be deleted
- `TrimLayer.spriteId` renamed to `textureId` (no trim material suffix)
- `ArmorRenderContext#submit` takes a `UvMapping`; added `glintPending()` / `submitPendingGlint()`
- Glow and radiant layers work with Improved Transparency
- Geo armor follows Entity Model Features player animations again (Fresh Animations Player, Entity Player Compat)
- Geo armor no longer shows in first person during Better Combat animations

releases.notes:
# 1.0.0

Port of 1.0.0 to Minecraft 1.20.1 (Fabric + Forge 47). Same feature set; no functional changes.

- Forge replaces NeoForge: the armor hook is a mixin on `ArmorFeatureRenderer#renderArmor`
- Dye color read through `DyeableItem`, trims through the stack's `Trim` NBT
- Shader awareness gates on Iris (Fabric) or Oculus (Forge)

Initial release.

- Renders Bedrock/GeckoLib geo armor models through the vanilla armor pipeline
- Armor bone convention with boot bones and a chest-anchored waist bone
- Armor trims with per-set trim textures, with greyscale fallback for third-party trim materials
- Emissive glowmasks (AzureLib `_glowmask` convention) and a radiant glow mode that feeds shader-pack bloom

mods.name: Armor Model API
mods.description: Renders Bedrock/GeckoLib geo armor models through the vanilla armor pipeline.

releases.notes:
# 1.1.0

- Per-item model and texture overrides through the vanilla `minecraft:custom_data` component
  (`{armor_model_api:{model, texture, glowmask, trim}}`), settable by commands, loot tables,
  recipes and datapacks - no custom component, the library stays client-side
- A stack naming both `model` and `texture` takes over an item nobody registered (any vanilla or
  third-party armor piece), with a default glow + trim pass stack
- `ArmorRenderContext` carries the base texture in effect (`texture()`) and the stack's `overrides()`;
  layers deriving assets from the base texture should read it from there
